summary: The OpenAPI Specification defines a standard, language-agnostic way to describe an interface to a Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) API, so that people and programs can understand a service without reading its source code. It covers the structure of that description well: server addresses, declared security schemes, data schemas built as a superset of JSON Schema, extension fields, and references that may span several documents. It leaves the wire protocol, the scenes, avatars and worlds that a service might carry, and a conformance test procedure to other work. A trap for a standards audience: only the major and minor version name the feature set, tools are told not to distinguish patch versions, and low-impact breaking changes may still arrive in a minor version. A second trap is that how implicit connections between documents of a multi-document description are resolved is left implementation-defined, so two tools can legitimately disagree.

When properly defined, a consumer can understand and interact with the remote service by parsing and serializing HTTP messages to and from a data model with a minimal amount of implementation logic.

coverage.note: The Info Object and Tag Object attach structured descriptive fields to an API description and its operations, which another tool can read. The part missing is scene content: the properties describe an API, not a scene or its parts.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.2.1, section 4.2 Info Object
sources.quote: The object provides metadata about the API.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.2.1, section 4.1.1 OpenAPI Object, Fixed Fields
sources.quote: A list of tags used by the OpenAPI Description with additional metadata. The order of the tags can be used to reflect on their order by the parsing tools. Not all tags that are used by the Operation Object must be declared. The tags that are not declared MAY be organized randomly or based on the tools’ logic. Each tag name in the list MUST be unique.

coverage.note: Preview image for an asset concerns scene content; the specification only defines an interface description for HTTP APIs, so this capability falls outside it.
